standard_prerequisites.name: The map K^{-1} tensor^L R' -> K^{-1} tensor R' is an isomorphism on cohomology in degree 0 and zero on H^{-1}, so the naive tensor complex agrees with the derived one in the degrees relevant to the truncation
standard_prerequisites.use: Concludes that the naive tensor product complex represents the truncation of the derived base change.

core_obligations: Record the distinguished triangle K^0 -> K^bullet -> K^{-1}[1] -> K^0[1] associated with the two-term complex representing K, and apply the base change functor to obtain a morphism of distinguished triangles comparing the derived tensor products with the naive tensor product complex (proof lines 22530-22546).

Observe that the two outer vertical arrows in that morphism are isomorphisms, because K^0 is flat, so that the naive complex K^0 tensor R' -> K^bullet tensor R' agrees with the derived base change in the relevant degrees (proof lines 22547).

Use that K^{-1} tensor^L R' -> K^{-1} tensor R' is an isomorphism on cohomology in degree 0 and that the higher cohomology of the naive complex vanishes above degree 0, to conclude that K^bullet tensor R' represents the truncation in degrees at least -1 of the derived base change (proof lines 22548-22549).
proof_roadmap: Rewrite the object K through the distinguished triangle of its two-term complex and base change the triangle along R -> R' (proof lines 22530-22546).
Use flatness of K^0 to see that the two outer arrows of the comparison map are isomorphisms (proof lines 22547).
Read off that the naive tensor product complex computes the truncation of the derived base change in degrees at least -1 (proof lines 22548-22549).
difficulty_reason: The statement fixes an object K of D(R) whose cohomology is concentrated in degrees -1 and 0, chooses a two-term complex K^{-1} -> K^0 representing it with K^0 flat, and asserts that the naive tensor product complex K^bullet tensor_R R' represents the truncation in degrees at least -1 of the derived base change (statement lines 22519-22527). The proof is a comparison of distinguished triangles rather than a computation: the base-changed triangle has the derived tensor products, the second triangle has the naive tensor products, the comparison map between them has isomorphisms on the two outer vertices precisely because K^0 is flat, and the remaining input is that the lowest term K^{-1} agrees with its derived tensor product in degree 0 (proof lines 22530-22549). The non-routine part is knowing which truncation is obtained, which is what the careful reading of the second triangle in degrees at least -1 provides.
